claims.text: Broadening the alloy's elemental mix increases its configurational entropy.
Increased configurational entropy promotes a uniform disordered microstructure.
A uniform disordered microstructure favors robust electron-phonon coupling.
Robust electron-phonon coupling stabilizes the superconducting state and makes Tc less sensitive to pressure-induced perturbations.
The baseline HEA has a relatively narrow elemental mix, lower configurational entropy, and unoptimized superconducting behavior.
Additional elements can be introduced within the same phase space to maximize configurational entropy without producing secondary phases.
The tested alloy can remain bcc or FCC with minimal secondary-phase precipitation from ambient pressure to approximately 35 GPa.
XRD and TEM can be used to verify the proposed uniform disordered microstructure and phase state.
Increased configurational entropy homogenizes the alloy's electronic environment.
A homogenized electronic environment stabilizes the electron-phonon interactions responsible for superconductivity.
The higher-entropy alloy will exhibit either a higher Tc or a Tc that is nearly invariant with pressure relative to the baseline alloy.
Increasing configurational entropy will produce corresponding changes in superconducting anisotropy.
Superconducting anisotropy can be estimated from resistivity measurements under magnetic fields of varying orientation and magnitude.
Above approximately 35 GPa, phase changes or competing phenomena may obscure the influence of configurational entropy on superconductivity.
A lack of statistically significant Tc enhancement or pressure robustness in the higher-entropy alloy relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
